messages:
ana: FYI starting POC with Kepler Health — they want to test Kepler-20b-quant-v2 for triage summarization. Primary asks: private deployment, KMS, and variant that supports prefix KV cache. Can SEs confirm compatibility?
ravi: On it. Quick Q: are they planning stream responses or batch inferencing?
ana: (typo) ana: sorry, batch inference mostly, but a few endpoints need low-latency streaming for triage UI.
ravi: OK. Kepler-20b-quant-v2 supports KV cache but streaming on quantized variants has known latency edge-cases. Need to pin sequence length.
lena: adding notes — model was quantized with 4-bit group-wise quant. Filtering & KV cache should be fine, but we saw reorder penalty when kv shard across hosts. For streaming we recommend a single-worker pin or small batch window.
derek: infra note: private deployment + KMS is fine, but Dedicated/private images currently ship kepler-20b-quant-v2 as a single-node fallback only. Autoscale for batch is OK, but streaming SLOs need reserved capacity.
maria: security checklist: they want SOC2 + custom questionnaire. Also asking whether the private run stores logs in customer S3 or our audit store?
ana: they asked for customer-managed KMS and logs to their S3.
maria: Customer-managed KMS yes, that’s supported for Private. Logs can be forwarded to customer S3 via our log-forwarder, but we need to confirm retention & PII redaction controls in the questionnaire. I can start a draft for the security answers.
ravi: For model compatibility, two actionable items: 1) We need a small test image with KV cache enabled and memory profile validated for 4-bit quant. 2) Provide a sample rollout config that pins model variant for streaming endpoints. I can prepare a repro and a short runbook.
lena: Also flagging tokenizer differences — Kepler uses byte-level merges; embedding hashes differ slightly. For their retrieval pipeline we should run an embed consistency check. If they rely on off-the-shelf embedding parity, we might need a conversion shim.
derek: Ops question: what commit window for the POC? If they want reserved nodes for streaming, pricing changes (reserved capacity) vs pay-as-you-go. Sales, confirm expected QPS/latency target so we can estimate cost.
ana: They asked for 50 rps sustained on streaming endpoints with p99 < 250ms, plus batch throughput for nightly offline runs.
ravi: 50rps + p99 250ms on quantized 20b is tight but achievable with pinned workers and KV cache warm-up. We'll propose Dedicated reserved set with warm standby.
maria: I'll attach the security questionnaire draft in a sec. Also need to know whether model weights are considered customer IP or third-party — legal will need that for the contract.
ana: Model is third-party open-source licensed, customer will fine-tune. Legal flagged derivative clause.
lena: For the onboarding test, I'll run three short evals: 1) embed parity vs reference, 2) KV cache hit-miss throughput, 3) streamed token latency at 512 seq. Expect results in ~48h.
ravi: I'll add a config snippet for the streaming pin. Example: 
```
rollout: 
  strategy: pin
  variant: kepler-20b-quant-v2
  workers: 2
  reserve: true
  kv_cache: enabled
```
Send this to infra to provision.
derek: Received — I'll provision a 2-node reserved pool for the POC. Pricing delta: add ~$18k/month for reserved streaming pool (prelim). Need sales to sign off.
nana: noted, I'll include pricing in the deck. Can SEs produce the eval artifacts and the runbook by Thursday?
ravi: Yes, eval artifacts + runbook by Thursday EOD.
lena: I'll push the tests tonight, share logs in the POC workspace.
maria: Draft questionnaire uploaded: https://redwood-internal/drive/kepler-poc-sec-qna — please review answers.
deploy-bot: Deployment request queued for reserved pool provisioning (request-id: rq_8842).
derek: Deploy queued, I'll follow up when nodes are live.
ana: Thanks team — I'll sync with the customer and loop back with legal for license clarifications. :thumbsup:
